findings.reason: unless the node places the geometry correction upstream of the digest (or extends the key over the refinement and the coil cache), a rebuild silently serves the pre-repair matrix and §7's guarantee "A rebuild then never reads a pre-repair matrix" is false while its negative control still passes.
findings.text: §7 asserts the geometry repair is automatically keyed ("a corrected jacket geometry changes the conductor columns the key already covers"), but `build.py` derives the sectioned-set digest from the PRE-refinement source columns and source polygon vertices plus the subdivision parameters only (`scripts/iter_sectioned_conductor_set/build.py:230-239`), while the geometry the build actually links is produced downstream by `subdivide_passive_thickness` (`build.py:222`) — and §7's own check (1) compares "the jacket and conductor polygons of VSU and VSL", the refinement's output. A correction landing in the refinement leaves the digest unchanged, so the cache-hit branch (`build.py:242-248`) loads the pre-repair `linkage.npy` wholesale and the repaired geometry never reaches the matrix; the coil block is cached under a separate key again (`build.py:262-268`, tag `b"finite-source:6"`) whose load validates only shape, not positivity.

findings.reason: a node on §6 check 3 dispatched after §7's key change (or one on §7 against §6's pre-change key) builds and measures against an entry the other node invalidated, so the two must be ordered or §7 must state that it supersedes §6's remaining check.
findings.text: §7 requires the repair to change the sectioned-set key and to hand power_convertor a new key, and §6 line 191 says "If the key derivation for new entries has to change, power_convertor is told the new key before the change merges"; yet §6 is itself still `implementable` with check 3 pending against that same cache, and neither section declares an ordering between them.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `scripts/iter_sectioned_conductor_set/build.py` and `guard_positive_definite` (`nova/circuit/linkage.py:291`) resolve, `linkage.npy` is the file `build.py` writes (line 241), and "the 12 mm and 6 mm sets" resolve to real cache keys (`scripts/iter_vessel_evolution/evolve.py`, 0.006 → 2163 passive circuits).
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §7's three clauses are measurable (split a stated 6.6e-5 excess, a positive-definiteness result, a delivered plant entry and key) and the section names a literal negative control that can fail on the unfixed code ("revert the repair, and the Schur complement again has the two negative eigenvalues").
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the only artefact locations §7 names are the durable in-repo caches (`.cache/iter-passive-plasma-circuit/sectioned-conductor-set/<digest>/`, `linkage.npy`), consistent with the declared gate-log location under `.cache/iter-passive-plasma-circuit/gate-logs/`, which exists; no session scratchpad or node-local temp path is named.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §7's prose names mechanisms (`guard_positive_definite`, the finite-source linkage, the Schur complement) rather than plan labels; no ticket number or stage name appears in the section text.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §7's mechanism for propagating the geometry repair into the cache does not run on the path the key covers.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §7 states one goal in its heading (make the coil and passive linkage positive definite); attribution, repair and hand-off are the steps of that one deliverable.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §7 changes the sectioned-set cache key but declares no relationship to §6, whose pending check 3 and whose "power_convertor is told the new key before the change merges" clause both run on that same key (snapshot lines 189–191, 195).
